persona: Solo life/business coach running 5-30 active clients over video calls

persona: Coach who has a great client result but hasn't turned it into something to show future prospects
title: I have an amazing client result - how do I turn it into a case study I can use in sales conversations?
workflowSummary: You describe the client's starting point, what you did together, and the result, and Venngage's AI structures it into a polished case study with a problem/solution/results narrative, which you can export as a PDF or slide to show skeptical prospects during a sales conversation.
samplePrompt: Turn this into a case study: client started at [starting point], we worked on [what you did], and the result was [measurable outcome]. Structure it as problem, approach, and results, and include a pull-quote from their testimonial.
beginnerNote: guided prompt-based workflow, no design skill needed.
pricingNote: Free tool available - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public product page.

persona: New or established coach who isn't sure what to actually charge for a package
title: I don't know what to charge for my coaching package and keep guessing
workflowSummary: You enter your income goal, expected client load, and delivery model, and the calculator shows what to charge per session or per package to hit that goal, alongside typical rate ranges for your coaching niche as a sanity check.
samplePrompt: Not a prompt-based tool - fill in: income goal, number of active clients you can realistically hold, and sessions per client per month. The calculator returns a suggested package price.
beginnerNote: fill-in-the-blank calculator, no coaching business background needed.
pricingNote: Free - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article with an embedded free calculator tool.

persona: Coach launching a new cohort or group program who wants real urgency without sounding sleazy
title: I'm opening enrollment for a new cohort - how do I write launch emails that create urgency honestly?
workflowSummary: You give Claude your real enrollment details - actual spot count, actual close date - and it drafts the classic 5-email launch arc (announcement, doors open, proof, objection-handling, final countdown), built only around urgency that's true, not manufactured scarcity.
samplePrompt: I'm opening enrollment for Cohort 7 of my group coaching program: 15 spots, doors close March 10. Write a 5-email launch sequence (announce, open cart, share proof, handle objections, final countdown) using only real details - no fake urgency.
beginnerNote: just requires having real enrollment details to plug in.
pricingNote: Free tier available; paid tier for higher usage - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public reference document on ethical scarcity/urgency patterns; illustrates the framework rather than being a product page.

persona: Coach juggling several prospects at different stages who has no idea what their actual close rate is
title: How do I keep track of every prospect I'm talking to without paying for a full CRM?
workflowSummary: Airtable's free Sales Pipeline template gives you a ready-made board with stages (Lead, Call Booked, Proposal Sent, Closed), so you can drag each prospect across stages and see your real close rate at a glance, without setting up or paying for a full CRM.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Duplicate the Sales Pipeline template, and add my current prospects with a status of Lead, Call Booked, Proposal Sent, or Closed so I can see where each one stands and calculate my close rate.
beginnerNote: pre-built template, just add your own leads.
pricingNote: Free to use the template on a free Airtable account - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public product page.

persona: Coach who runs a free webinar or masterclass to sell a program but sales taper off after the live event
title: I ran a free training and got a lot of registrants - how do I actually turn them into paying clients?
workflowSummary: EverWebinar turns your recorded training into an always-on funnel, running it on a schedule with live-feeling chat and polls, and automatically sends different follow-up emails to attendees, early exits, and no-shows so each group gets a message suited to how engaged they actually were.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Schedule my recorded masterclass to run daily at multiple times, and send 3 different follow-up sequences based on whether someone attended fully, left early, or didn't show up.
beginnerNote: the automated funnel setup takes real time to configure well, per independent reviews.
pricingNote: Around $99/month - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public product page.

persona: Coach whose prospect booked a free discovery call and then simply didn't show up
title: Someone no-showed my free discovery call - how do I get them to rebook without sounding annoyed?
workflowSummary: You describe that the prospect no-showed, and ChatGPT drafts a short, warm message that assumes good intent (life happens) and makes it easy to rebook with one click, instead of a message that reads as passive-aggressive or guilt-tripping.
samplePrompt: A prospect no-showed our discovery call today. Write a short, warm follow-up message that assumes something came up, includes my booking link to rebook, and doesn't sound annoyed or guilt-trippy.
beginnerNote: just describe the situation.
pricingNote: Free tier available; paid tier for higher usage - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article on follow-up email etiquette and cadence; not coaching-specific, but the tone guidance applies directly.

persona: Coach with multiple program tiers (e.g. self-study, group, 1:1 VIP) who wants prospects to easily compare and choose
title: I have 3 pricing tiers for my program - how do I show prospects the difference clearly?
workflowSummary: Describe your 3 program tiers and what's included in each, and Canva's Magic Design generates a clean comparison one-pager with columns for each tier, which you can edit and send alongside a proposal or add to your sales page.
samplePrompt: Create a 3-column comparison one-pager for my coaching tiers: Self-Study ($297), Group Coaching ($1,500), and VIP 1:1 ($5,000), listing what's included in each and highlighting the VIP tier as the recommended option.
beginnerNote: describe what you want in plain language, layouts generate automatically.
pricingNote: Free plan available (limited monthly AI credits); Pro ~$15/month unlocks more credits - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public independent review; reconfirm current AI credit limits and pricing on Canva's own pricing page.

persona: Coach who has never written a real sales page for their paid program and is staring at a blank page
title: I need to write an actual sales page for my coaching program and don't know where to start
workflowSummary: Jasper's AIDA (Attention, Interest, Desire, Action) template walks you through your offer, audience, and tone, then drafts a full sales page - headline, benefits, testimonials section, and a call to action - that you edit and publish rather than writing from a blank page.
samplePrompt: Using the AIDA framework, write a sales page for my coaching program: [program name], for [audience], solving [core problem], priced at [price]. Include a headline, 3 benefit sections, a spot for testimonials, and a clear call to action.
beginnerNote: guided templates, no copywriting background needed.
pricingNote: Paid plans only, from around $49/month; free trial may be available - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog post on vendor's domain.

persona: Coach running a group or cohort program who wants members to connect with each other between live calls
title: I want a private space where my group coaching members can talk to each other between our calls
workflowSummary: Circle gives each cohort its own branded space for discussion, resources, and events, with course content that can drip on a schedule tied to that specific intake - so a new cohort gets its own room instead of mixing in with members from an earlier round.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Create a dedicated Space for Cohort 4 with a discussion feed, a resources area, and a course area that drips content weekly, separate from the Cohort 3 space.
beginnerNote: powerful once set up, but the space/course structure takes real planning up front.
pricingNote: Plans vary; check circle.so/pricing for current tiers - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Independent comparison article; reconfirm current features and pricing on Circle's own site.

persona: Coach running a live cohort where everyone needs to be on the same lesson at the same time for calls to make sense
title: How do I make sure everyone in my cohort sees each week's material on the same day, no matter when they signed up?
workflowSummary: Kajabi's 'Drip by Specific Date' setting releases each module on the same calendar date for every member regardless of when they enrolled, so your live call each week lines up with what everyone just unlocked instead of some members being ahead or behind.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Set Module 1 to unlock March 3rd, Module 2 to unlock March 10th, and Module 3 to unlock March 17th for everyone in this cohort, regardless of enrollment date.
beginnerNote: the setting itself is simple, but planning the calendar around your live call schedule takes some upfront thought.
pricingNote: Cohort-based course feature requires Growth or Pro plan - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog post on vendor's domain.

persona: Coach who runs the same 8-week program multiple times a year and now has 2-3 cohorts active at once
title: I have two cohorts of the same program running at the same time - how do I keep their content and calls from getting mixed up?
workflowSummary: Kajabi's Cohorts Index page lists every active cohort of a program separately, each with its own member list, drip schedule, and certificates, so Spring Cohort and Summer Cohort stay fully separate even though they're running the same curriculum at once.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Create a second cohort of this program for our Summer intake, with its own drip schedule starting June 1st, kept separate from the Spring cohort already in progress.
beginnerNote: the cohort structure itself is straightforward, but requires the Growth or Pro plan to access.
pricingNote: Cohort-based course feature requires Growth or Pro plan - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public help-center article on vendor's domain.

persona: Coach whose group program members log in once and never come back
title: How do I keep my group program members actually engaged instead of joining once and disappearing?
workflowSummary: Skool's built-in points system and leaderboards give members visible progress and light competition just for participating and completing lessons, without you having to build a rewards system yourself - creators running cohort programs report better completion rates because of it.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Turn on Skool's points and leaderboard for this community, awarding points for posting, commenting, and completing each module.
beginnerNote: the gamification is built in and turns on with a toggle, no setup required.
pricingNote: Paid plans only, check skool.com/pricing for current rates - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Independent comparison article; reconfirm current features and pricing on Skool's own site.

persona: Coach who wants clients to finish their program feeling recognized, not just done
title: I want to give my clients a certificate when they finish my coaching program
workflowSummary: You describe the program and what completing it means, and Certifier's AI drafts the certificate wording and layout, which you can save as a reusable template so every future cohort graduate gets one automatically without you redesigning it each time.
samplePrompt: Create a certificate for completing my 12-week 'Confident Leader' group coaching program, dated for this cohort's graduation, with a spot for the recipient's name and my signature.
beginnerNote: describe the certificate in plain language, no design skill needed.
pricingNote: Free AI certificate generator; paid plans for reusable templates and bulk sending - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public product page.

persona: Coach managing 10-30 group program clients who can't personally check in with each one daily between sessions
title: I want my whole group of clients to check in on their commitments daily, not just during our sessions
workflowSummary: GroupHabits gives your whole roster a shared live feed where every client logs their daily check-in and can see (and react to) everyone else's, so accountability happens continuously between sessions instead of only during the time you personally have with each client.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Set up a daily check-in feed for this cohort where each member logs one action toward their program goal, visible to the whole group with reactions enabled.
beginnerNote: browser-based, no app download required for members to start checking in.
pricingNote: Not confirmed in source - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog post on vendor's domain; written for personal trainers, but the same one-to-many accountability model applies directly to group coaching.

persona: Coach whose group call replays sit in a video library that members rarely go back and watch
title: How do I make my group call replays easier for busy clients to actually go back and review?
workflowSummary: Hello Audio turns your recorded group coaching calls into a private podcast feed members can subscribe to in their own podcast app, so they can relisten to a session while driving or walking instead of needing to sit down and rewatch a video.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Upload this week's group call recording to a private podcast feed for this cohort only, with an episode title summarizing what we covered.
beginnerNote: designed specifically for course creators and group coaches turning existing recordings into audio.
pricingNote: Not confirmed in source - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public product page.

persona: Coach halfway through a group program who wants to know how it's landing before it's too late to adjust
title: I want to check in with my whole cohort partway through the program to see how it's going
workflowSummary: Typeform's coaching feedback template gives you a ready-made short survey to send at the midpoint of a program, asking how the experience and progress feel so far, so you can adjust pacing or content before the program ends instead of only finding out what worked in a final review.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Customize the Coaching Feedback Form template into a 4-question midpoint pulse check: how supported they feel, what's working, what's not, and one thing they wish we covered.
beginnerNote: ready-made template, just customize the questions.
pricingNote: Free tier available with response limits; paid plans for more responses - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public template page.

persona: Coach whose clients finish a great program and then disappear, losing the relationship and future referrals
title: My program just ended - how do I keep past clients connected instead of losing touch with them completely?
workflowSummary: A coach running a 10-week program invited graduates into a dedicated alumni space inside their Mighty Network after their cohort ended, giving them continued community and connection instead of the relationship simply stopping - the same structure that's led repeat members to apply for a program again.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Create an alumni space for graduates of this program, separate from active cohort members, where they can stay connected and hear about future offers.
beginnerNote: the community structure itself is straightforward, but deciding what ongoing value to offer alumni takes planning.
pricingNote: Not confirmed in source - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public case study on vendor's domain describing a real coaching-group alumni implementation.

persona: Coach running a group coaching call who wants people to actually talk to each other, not just listen
title: I want to break my group call into smaller discussion groups instead of everyone just listening to me
workflowSummary: Zoom lets you split a group coaching call into smaller breakout rooms for a discussion or paired accountability exercise, then bring everyone back to the main room to share - a simple way to make a mastermind-style call feel participatory instead of one-directional.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Split today's group call into breakout rooms of 3-4 people for a 10-minute discussion on this week's topic, then bring everyone back to share one takeaway.
beginnerNote: breakout rooms are a built-in meeting feature, no extra setup needed beyond enabling them.
pricingNote: Breakout rooms included in Zoom Meetings on paid plans - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article specifically about using Zoom breakout rooms for mastermind/group coaching.

persona: Executive coach starting a new engagement with a corporate leader who wants a baseline read on how the leader is perceived
title: I want to run a real 360-degree feedback assessment for my executive client without hiring a separate consultant
workflowSummary: Launch-360 is a plug-and-play 360 platform built specifically for coaches - you select from six research-backed leadership competencies (executive presence, staff management, communication, etc.), invite the client's raters, and get a report you can walk through in a single debrief session, no consultants or certifications required.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Launch a 360 assessment for [client name] covering executive presence, communication, and relationship management, with raters including their manager, 3 peers, and 2 direct reports.
beginnerNote: built for coaches specifically, no installation or consultant needed to launch.
pricingNote: Not confirmed in source - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog post on vendor's domain. 360 feedback involves other people's opinions about the client - agree on confidentiality and anonymity rules with the client and sponsor before launching.

persona: Executive coach whose client keeps clashing with a particular stakeholder (manager, peer, or board member) due to a communication style mismatch
title: My client and their manager keep talking past each other - how do I help my client understand how to communicate with them?
workflowSummary: Crystal predicts a person's DISC-based communication style from public professional data and generates practical guidance on how to adapt tone and approach for them, which you can use to help your client prepare for a specific meeting with a stakeholder whose style differs from their own.
samplePrompt: My client is a [DISC type] working with a manager who tends to be [direct/analytical/etc.]. Give me 3 practical adjustments my client could make in how they present ideas to this person.
beginnerNote: Chrome extension overlays insights directly on LinkedIn profiles, minimal setup.
pricingNote: Free plan (5 profile credits); Premium ~$49/month (annual) - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Independent tool directory listing; reconfirm current pricing on Crystal's own site. Predicting a real person's personality from public data without their knowledge raises its own consent considerations worth discussing with your client.

persona: Executive coach who has assessment and 360 results for a client but needs to turn them into an actual development roadmap
title: I have my client's assessment results - how do I turn them into a real development plan instead of just a debrief conversation?
workflowSummary: You feed ClickUp Brain your client's role, strengths, development areas, and goals, and it drafts a structured individual development plan with milestones and suggested learning activities, which then stays linked to tasks and check-ins so the plan evolves as the engagement progresses instead of sitting in a static document.
samplePrompt: Create a 6-month individual development plan for a [role] transitioning into [new responsibility]. Strengths: [list]. Development areas: [list]. Include 60-day and 120-day milestones and suggested development activities for each area.
beginnerNote: drafts the plan quickly, but you'll want to customize activities to match your own coaching methodology.
pricingNote: Free to start; paid plans for full ClickUp Brain features - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public product page.

persona: Executive coach whose corporate sponsor (HR or L&D) wants to see evidence the coaching engagement is working, not just that sessions happened
title: My client's company wants a report showing the coaching is actually working, not just a list of session dates
workflowSummary: Delenta centralizes session logs, goal tracking, and engagement data on one platform and can generate a sponsor-facing report - engagement themes, completion rates, and progress against the original goals - so building a credible impact report takes minutes instead of hours of manual write-up.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Generate a quarterly sponsor report for [client]'s engagement showing sessions completed, progress against the 3 goals set at kickoff, and overall engagement health, without including session content details.
beginnerNote: the reporting is automated once session data is logged consistently, but requires adopting the platform for day-to-day session tracking first.
pricingNote: Not confirmed in source - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog post on vendor's domain. A sponsor report should never include the substance of what was discussed in sessions - agree on what's shareable with the client and sponsor before the engagement starts.

persona: Executive coach helping a client prepare for a high-stakes board presentation or leadership town hall
title: My client has a huge presentation to the board coming up - how do I help them rehearse it properly?
workflowSummary: Yoodli runs a live AI roleplay where your client can rehearse their presentation or Q&A out loud, then get feedback on pacing, filler words, and clarity - useful as homework between sessions so your client walks into the real board meeting having already rehearsed under some pressure.
samplePrompt: Roleplay a board presentation Q&A where the AI plays a skeptical board member asking pointed follow-up questions about [topic]. Score the response on clarity and confidence afterward.
beginnerNote: free tier included; guided roleplay format works for presentation practice as well as conversations.
pricingNote: Free tier (5 lifetime sessions); Pro from $8/month, Advanced from $20/month (annual billing) - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public product page.

persona: Executive coach kicking off a new corporate engagement who needs to understand the client's context before session one
title: I'm about to start coaching a new executive client - what should I ask their manager and peers before our first session?
workflowSummary: You describe the client's role and why the coaching was commissioned, and Claude drafts a short set of stakeholder interview questions for the client's manager or sponsor - covering what success looks like, specific behaviors to watch for, and any context the coach should know - so the kickoff call has real structure instead of an open-ended chat.
samplePrompt: I'm starting an executive coaching engagement with a [role] whose manager requested coaching because of [reason]. Draft 6 stakeholder interview questions for a 30-minute alignment call with the manager before session one.
beginnerNote: just requires describing the context honestly.
pricingNote: Free tier available; paid tier for higher usage - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article describing the importance of pre-engagement baseline and stakeholder alignment in corporate coaching; not a product page for Claude itself.

persona: Executive coach whose client has a difficult conversation coming up (a hard feedback conversation, a conflict with a peer, or a layoff)
title: My client has to deliver really difficult news to their team - how do I help them prepare what to say?
workflowSummary: You describe the situation and what your client needs to communicate, and Claude drafts talking points that are direct and honest without being harsh - a starting point your client can adapt into their own words rather than reading verbatim, which you then review together in session.
samplePrompt: My client needs to tell a direct report their role is being eliminated in a reorg. Draft compassionate but direct talking points for this conversation: the news itself, why it's happening, and what support is available, without over-apologizing or being vague.
beginnerNote: just requires describing the situation clearly; review the output together in session rather than having the client read it verbatim.
pricingNote: Free tier available; paid tier for higher usage - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public blog article on structuring hard messages clearly; not specific to executive coaching, but the plain-and-direct framing applies. This task involves sensitive personnel matters - never include the employee's real name or identifying details in the prompt.

persona: Executive coach pitching a coaching engagement to a corporate HR or L&D buyer, not an individual paying client
title: I need to send a formal proposal to a company's HR department for an executive coaching engagement, not just a quote for a private client
workflowSummary: Paste your scoping call notes into Proposify's editor, and its AI drafts a formal statement-of-work style proposal - engagement objectives, session cadence, measurement approach, and pricing - built for a corporate procurement or HR audience rather than an individual consumer.
samplePrompt: Turn these scoping notes into a proposal for [company]'s HR department: coaching [number] of leaders over [timeframe], including kickoff stakeholder interviews, monthly sponsor check-ins, and a final impact report. Include pricing per leader and as a program total.
beginnerNote: the AI drafts content well, but a corporate-facing proposal template takes more setup than a consumer one.
pricingNote: Free AI proposal generator; paid plans for full platform features - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public product page.

persona: Executive coach juggling engagements across several different companies at once, each with its own sponsor and confidentiality boundaries
title: I'm coaching leaders at 4 different companies right now - how do I keep each engagement organized without mixing anything up?
workflowSummary: Coaching.com gives each engagement its own branded client portal, session notes, and goal tracking, with role-based access so a sponsor only ever sees what's meant for them - keeping four separate corporate engagements cleanly siloed instead of relying on folders and memory.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Set up a new engagement workspace for [Company D], with its own branded portal, goal tracker, and sponsor-visible dashboard kept separate from my other 3 active company engagements.
beginnerNote: powerful once set up, but structuring engagement templates and access rules takes upfront work.
pricingNote: Not confirmed in source - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public product page.

persona: Executive coach who needs to keep detailed session notes for their own use while sharing only high-level progress with the sponsor
title: How do I keep my private coaching notes secure and separate from what I share with my client's company?
workflowSummary: Simply.Coach is SOC2, HIPAA, and GDPR-compliant coaching software with role-based permissions, so you can keep your private session notes visible only to you while a separate, sponsor-facing view shows only the high-level progress data the company is entitled to see.
samplePrompt: Setup task: Set my detailed session notes to private (coach-only visibility), and configure the sponsor dashboard to show only goal progress and session completion, not note content.
beginnerNote: the compliance and permission structure is a real strength, but takes deliberate configuration to use correctly.
pricingNote: Not confirmed in source - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Public product page. Confirm the specific compliance certifications (SOC2, HIPAA, GDPR) are still current and relevant to your jurisdiction before relying on them for sensitive client data.
